issue_context.title: Force upgrade extension should override pinned versions
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

I would expect running upgrade with `--force` to override a pinned extension

```bash
$ gh extension upgrade ext-name --force               
X Failed upgrading extension ext-name: pinned extensions can not be upgraded
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. install a pinned extension that is not the latest version, e.g. `gh extension install ext-name-url --pin some_version`
2. run `gh extension upgrade ext-name --force`
3. See error

### Expected vs actual behavior

The effect of `--force` isn't clear from the output of the help command, this may be the intended behavior but I did find it surprising. Changing the value of `ispinned:` to `false` in the extension's manifest.yml file allow the upgrade to proceed, so this doesn't seem to be a technical limitation.

### Logs

N/A
comments: Good idea. We imagine that `gh ext upgrade --force` should un-pin the extension and allow it to upgrade.
@mislav is there anything else `--force` should do? I'll add it to the flag output

review_comments: removing `e.isPinned` here as it is checked just before this function is called in https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/ba1df3e6575a099fe89f1835f7abf2c7ae4b38dc/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L578

This may be a bit of scope creep, but since we are touching this method, it would be nice to add some unit tests for the new behavior so it does not get accidentally changed in the future. I know there are not tests for `UpdateAvailable()` yet, but seems like it would be fairly easy to add.
@samcoe I added unit tests in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/6513/commits/8a320b63d7beed1a10e3c2bf6cf60ac15debca9a not sure if that's what you had in mind?

this seemed the best test to duplicate, changing the pinned = true in `m.upgradeExtension(ext, true)`, rather than modify  `TestManager_UpgradeExtension_BinaryExtension` to have it implicitly test pinned = false
